learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze the darkest chapter in independent India's history: The declaration of the 1975 Emergency, the suspension of civil liberties, and the eventual triumph of democracy!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Economic hardship, student protests in Gujarat (Navnirman) and Bihar, a massive railway strike, and a conflict between the Government and the Judiciary created an atmosphere of extreme political instability.

Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) transformed the Bihar student protests into a nationwide political movement demanding 'Total Revolution' against Indira Gandhi's government, accusing it of corruption and authoritarianism.
Following an Allahabad High Court ruling that invalidated her 1971 election win, Indira Gandhi convinced the President to declare a national emergency, citing 'internal disturbances'.

Fundamental rights were suspended, opposition leaders were thrown in jail using preventive detention, and strict censorship was imposed on the press. Extra-constitutional powers were used for forced sterilizations and slum clearances.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🗳️ The 1977 Elections and the Janata Party
main_concepts.simple_explanation: When elections were finally called in 1977, the angry public heavily punished the Congress. A coalition of opposition parties formed the Janata Party, which formed the first non-Congress government at the center.

fun_activity.title: 🗞️ The Censored Newspaper
fun_activity.instructions: During the Emergency, newspapers left blank spaces where the government had censored articles. Take a short news article from today, use a black marker to cross out the 5 most important words, and see if the story still makes any sense!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the date: June 25, 1975. It is a critical milestone in Indian political history.
📌 Always mention 'Preventive Detention'—the power used by the government to arrest people without trial to prevent them from committing a crime.
📌 Be ready to discuss the Shah Commission, which was set up by the Janata Party to investigate the abuses committed during the Emergency.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Allahabad High Court judgment by Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha invalidated Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election on grounds of electoral malpractice.
⭐ The 42nd Amendment was passed during the Emergency, heavily concentrating power in the hands of the executive.
⭐ The Emergency proved that while Indian democracy can be temporarily derailed, the democratic spirit of the Indian voters is incredibly resilient.
